problem: Existing token-caching methods for VLA/VLM inference assume a static camera view (same patch index = same content across frames) and ignore task progression. In VLN, continuous ego-motion displaces tokens so position-wise matching pairs misaligned content, and token relevance shifts with instruction stage so visually stable cached tokens go stale.
motivation: Large VLM/VLA-based VLN planners need a full forward pass at every step, so per-step latency blocks real-time robot deployment. Analysis on VLN trajectories shows view-aligned matching gives ~10.3% higher cross-frame token similarity than position-wise matching, and instruction-conditioned attention focus (Jaccard distance) shifts substantially across navigation phases even when appearance is stable.
key_idea: Training-free KV token caching for VLN that retrieves cached tokens via depth/pose-based view-aligned remapping and vetoes reuse for tokens whose instruction-conditioned relevance is high or rapidly changing, with an entropy-based per-layer reuse budget.
insight: Viewpoint shift displaces reusable content rather than destroying it, so fixing the retrieval index (k=0 falls back to position-wise reuse) recovers reuse without noise. Visual stability is necessary but not sufficient for reuse, so semantic vetoing is needed. Ablation (Table 2): removing view-aligned remap drops SR 63.1→62.4 at a similar or higher reuse ratio (43%); removing the semantic gate drops SR to 62.9; removing the visual gate drops SR to 61.7 with higher reuse (49%), below the no-cache baseline.
method: View-aligned remapping: back-project each token center with depth via intrinsics K, apply relative pose T_{t→t-1}, re-project to get correspondence π_t(i), with 3×3 neighborhood refinement (k=3).

Visual gate: a token is reusable only if π_t(i) lies inside the field of view and cosine similarity with the remapped previous token exceeds τ_vis (0.85); tokens without valid depth are always refreshed.
Semantic gate (hard veto): a token is force-refreshed if its instruction-conditioned relevance exceeds τ_abs (τ_s=0.70) or its change between steps exceeds τ_Δ.
Dual-aware mask: m = m_vis·(1−m_sem), i.e. strict AND of visual stability and semantic non-transition.

Cross-frame KV splice: at every decoder layer, reused tokens take K/V from the cache at π_t(i), the rest are computed fresh. All positions are filled, so there is no token dropping or irregular shapes, and RoPE is recomputed for the new positions.
Layer-adaptive policy: per-layer reuse ratio ρ = clip(ρ_max − α·H, ρ_min, ρ_max) with H the attention entropy (ρ_max=0.90); high-entropy layers reuse less.
Drop-in wrapper on the System-2 VLA planner, with a small on-device cache (~11.2 MB per frame).

setting.backbone: InternVLA-N1 / DualVLN System-2 planner (Qwen2.5-VL-7B, frozen, no fine-tuning)
setting.training_data: none (training-free); thresholds calibrated on a small held-out trajectory set
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D with relative camera pose (simulator or odometry)
setting.action_space: low-level continuous-environment actions generated autoregressively by the VLA planner (VLN-CE)
setting.privileged: depth and relative camera pose from the simulator/odometry are used for view-aligned remapping

numbers.extra: training-free caching on top of the frozen backbone; 1.52× step/episode speedup (637→419 ms/step, 31% token reuse) measured on a 10-episode pilot run on A100
numbers.evidence: Table 1: Comparison with VLN methods on R2R-CE; text 'achieving SR = 63.1 and SPL = 57.6'

numbers_note: Efficiency numbers (637 ms → 419 ms, 1.52×) come from a 10-episode pilot run, not the full split. Hyper-parameter sensitivity is only in figures. The paper does not state whether the 'zero_shot' label applies in a benchmark sense; it is training-free on top of a pre-trained backbone.
results: On R2R-CE val-unseen (1,839 episodes) VLN-Cache reaches SR 63.1 / SPL 57.6 / NE 3.93 versus the unmodified DualVLN baseline at 64.3 / 58.5 / 4.05, a 1.2-point SR drop. It gives a 1.52× step and episode speedup (637→419 ms/step, 31% average token reuse). Removing any component lowers SR to 61.7–62.9.
limitations: Requires depth and relative pose from the simulator or odometry; map-based navigation is not addressed.
Efficiency was measured on only a 10-episode pilot on a single A100 and only with InternVLA-N1 on R2R-CE, so the generality claim is untested; thresholds must be hand-tuned (no automatic selection).
Accuracy drops slightly relative to no-cache (SR −1.2), and the full ablation shows a speed-accuracy trade-off.
